Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Dev: i checked with the venue this morning. We can get in at 5:45 either way, but the custodian needs the room cleared by 9:30. The movie is 94 minutes, and with the intro + a short discussion we'd be done around 8:35 if we start at 6:45. 7:00 still fits too.

Inez: one wrinkle: the bus from east ridge gets to bay street at 6:28, then it's about a 7 min walk. Last month people were still finding seats after the welcome. If we start earlier, some folks could miss the first few minutes, unless we hold the intro til 7:00? not sure that solves it.

Cal: the youth event is in the room next door, not the library hall. Their coordinator told me, “we expect families to leave by 6:10, but a few may stay to stack chairs.” There's a shared lobby, so the noise could carry over while we're setting up. They aren't using our chairs.

Mara: thanks, that's useful. For context, our usual crowd is 25–35 people, and we have 32 chairs plus 8 folding ones in the storage closet. We haven't had to turn anyone away, but October's title has been getting more RSVPs than usual. I can bring the little sign-in table from home.

Jo: could we put the door sign outside the side entrance? The front path is partly blocked by the paving work, and last time two people went to the cafe entrance by mistake. Building staff said the side door is open until 7:15, but after that we need to meet late arrivals.

Inez: i can do that. Also the projector was fine at the last screening, though the HDMI cable only reached the front table if we moved the speaker stand. The venue has a 10-foot extension cord; Dev, do you know if we should bring our longer one too?

Dev: yeah, i'll bring the 25-foot cable and test it before doors. The sound was a little low during the opening credits in September, so I’ll bring the small mixer as well. We should keep the volume reasonable because the ceramics class is in the basement until 7:30.

Rafi: on refreshments, the grant covers up to $45, and we have $18 left from the last night. Tea, coffee, and popcorn came to $31 in August. I can pick those up, but do we still have compostable cups? I found one sleeve in the supply bin, maybe 40 cups.

Cal: i counted 36 cups yesterday, and the paper napkins are almost gone. There are 2 boxes of tea bags, but no coffee filters. If we buy filters and napkins, we should be near the same total as August. The bakery on Pine can donate day-old rolls, but they need a head count by Thursday.

Mara: let's avoid promising the rolls until we know how many are coming. The RSVP sheet has 29 names right now, including 6 people who asked for captions. The film file has English captions, and I checked that they display on the room's projector. We have 4 printed large-type programs left from September.

Jo: for the welcome, I can mention the bus stop, the side entrance, and that people can come and go quietly if they need to. Last time someone asked whether discussion was required, so i'll say it's optional. Is anyone planning to introduce the filmmaker, or should I stick to the two-sentence description from the program?

Dev: the filmmaker sent a short bio, but hasn't confirmed whether they're joining us remotely. I wouldn't advertise a Q&A yet. The bio says they grew up near the harbor and shot several scenes on the old ferry; I'll send the exact wording to Jo so we don't accidentally add details.

Inez: one small thing, the October calendar on the website says “doors at 6:30” and the printed flyers say “film at 7.” Neither mentions the poetry event. If we decide on a different time, someone will need to update both, plus the neighborhood email. Who has access to the calendar login?

Mara: i do, but before I edit anything, can you all weigh in on the start time? Specifically, would 6:45 be better than 7:00 given the youth event, the 6:28 bus, and the 9:30 room deadline? If we keep 7:00, I can ask the venue whether the lobby is available for early arrivals.

Rafi: one practical thought: if we keep doors at 6:30 and start at 7, people from the bus have about 25 minutes to get inside and settle. If doors move to 6:15, that gives early arrivals more time, but the poetry group may still be clearing the lobby. I don't know their exact finish time beyond what Cal heard.

Cal: same here, I only have the coordinator's estimate. I can message her tomorrow and ask whether the lobby will be clear by 6:15, and whether their families use the side entrance. I won't ask them to change their schedule; just trying to avoid sending our audience into a crowded doorway.

Jo: thanks. I can hold off on printing the welcome sheet until we settle the time. The printer at the center is low on blue ink, but black-and-white copies are readable. We need around 35, plus a few extra for walk-ins. The large-type programs can go on the sign-in table.

Mara: great, please reply here when you hear back. For now, the open items are:
1. confirm whether the lobby and side entrance are clear around 6:15;
2. choose a 6:45 or 7:00 film start;
3. check whether the bakery can provide rolls by Thursday;
4. update the website, flyers, and neighborhood email only if the time changes.

Dev: i'll bring the cables and mixer either way, and test the captions before doors. If the projector acts up, there’s a spare HDMI adapter in the labeled box under the sign-in table. I can arrive at 5:45, but I need to leave by 9:15 to catch the last northbound train.

Inez: i can stay for cleanup until 9:30, as long as we start packing the refreshments before the discussion ends. Does the custodian want the chairs stacked in rows of six again? They asked us to leave a clear aisle last time, but I can't remember if there was a specific arrangement.

Cal: i'll check the note from the custodian. I also have the folding-chair key, and can unlock the closet when I arrive.
